pharm: Tertiary-amine antispasmodic that relaxes gastrointestinal smooth muscle by a dual mechanism: antimuscarinic blockade at acetylcholine receptor sites and a direct (musculotropic) relaxant effect on smooth muscle.
quick: Start 20 mg four times daily; may increase to 40 mg four times daily after 1 week
May take before meals to relieve postprandial cramps
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Contraindicated in nursing mothers (apnea reported in infants)
Anticholinergic effects, heat intolerance, CNS/psychiatric effects in elderly
summary: Dicyclomine is an antispasmodic, antimuscarinic agent used to treat functional bowel/irritable bowel syndrome by relaxing gastrointestinal smooth muscle. It is contraindicated in infants under 6 months and in nursing mothers, and in glaucoma, obstructive GI/urinary disease, severe ulcerative colitis, reflux esophagitis, myasthenia gravis and unstable cardiovascular status. Anticholinergic effects, heat prostration, and confusion or delirium (especially in the elderly) can occur.
indications: Treatment of functional bowel / irritable bowel syndrome (intestinal hypermotility)

dosage.d: Increase to 40 mg four times a day if tolerated
dosage.n: Discontinue if efficacy not achieved at <80 mg/day after 2 weeks

dosage.d: 10-20 mg IM four times a day
dosage.t: Up to 1-2 days when oral not tolerated

admin: Take orally; the injectable form is for intramuscular use only and must never be given intravenously
Doses may be timed before meals to control postprandial cramping
Reassess after 2 weeks; discontinue if effective doses below 80 mg/day cannot control symptoms or side effects limit use
Use lower doses and caution in elderly patients (confusion, delirium risk)
Advise patients to avoid overheating/strenuous activity in hot weather (reduced sweating)
moa: Dicyclomine relieves smooth muscle spasm of the gastrointestinal tract through a dual mechanism. It exerts a specific antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) effect at acetylcholine receptor sites, with roughly one-eighth the milligram potency of atropine, and a direct musculotropic relaxant effect on smooth muscle, demonstrated by antagonism of bradykinin- and histamine-induced spasm. It has relatively little antimuscarinic effect on the eye and other organs at therapeutic doses compared with atropine.

absolute: Infants less than 6 months of age
Obstructive disease of the gastrointestinal tract
Unstable cardiovascular status in acute hemorrhage
relative: Hyperthyroidism, coronary heart disease, heart failure, tachyarrhythmia, hypertension

preg: Limited human data. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Contraindicated in nursing mothers. Dicyclomine is excreted in breast milk and infant apnea has been reported; do not use while breastfeeding.
renal: Limited data; use with caution in renal impairment as the drug is largely excreted in the urine.
hepatic: Limited data on metabolism; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Potassium chloride solid oral dosage forms (increased GI mucosal injury with slowed transit)
moderate: Antiglaucoma agents (antagonized; may raise intraocular pressure)
Antacids (reduce absorption of dicyclomine - separate dosing)
Drugs whose GI absorption is altered by slowed motility (e.g., digoxin)
interactions.food: May be taken before meals to control postprandial symptoms.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive drowsiness and CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Anticholinergic effect may delay gastric emptying and affect absorption-based tests.

serious: Heat prostration (fever and heat stroke from decreased sweating)
Curare-like neuromuscular blockade at high doses
rare: Apnea in infants (with exposure via breast milk)

monitoring: Anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, vision, urinary retention, constipation)
Mental status, particularly in elderly patients
Tolerance to heat / signs of heat prostration
counsel: May cause drowsiness, dizziness or blurred vision - use caution when driving
Avoid becoming overheated; you may sweat less, raising the risk of heat stroke in hot weather
Report confusion, agitation, fast heartbeat, difficulty urinating, or severe constipation
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
Do not take if you have glaucoma or urinary/bowel obstruction
pk: Plasma peak in 60-90 minutes after an oral dose
Initial elimination ~1.8 hours, with a longer secondary phase
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Dual antimuscarinic + direct musculotropic relaxant action on gut smooth muscle
Contraindicated in infants <6 months and in nursing mothers (infant apnea reported)
Anticholinergic burden - avoid or minimize in the elderly (confusion, delirium, falls)
Counsel on heat prostration: reduced sweating raises heat-stroke risk
Injectable form is intramuscular only; never give intravenously
missed: If a dose is missed, continue the normal dosing schedule; do not take a double dose to make up for it.
overdose: Features include headache, nausea, vomiting, blurred vision, dilated pupils, hot dry skin, dry mouth, difficulty swallowing, dizziness and CNS stimulation including convulsions; a curare-like neuromuscular blockade can cause weakness or paralysis. Contact a poison control center. Provide supportive care; consider physostigmine for severe central anticholinergic toxicity and respiratory support if paralysis occurs.
